back_blocks.md: A **disproportionation** reaction is one in which the same element is simultaneously **oxidised** and **reduced**. The reaction of chlorine with alkali is a classic example.

cards.back_md: A **disproportionation** reaction is one in which the same element is simultaneously **oxidised** and **reduced**. The reaction of chlorine with alkali is a classic example.

front_blocks.md: Write the ionic equation for the reaction of Cl<sub>2</sub> with cold dilute NaOH and identify which species is oxidised and which is reduced.

back_blocks.md: Cl<sub>2</sub> is **oxidised** to ClO<sup>-</sup> (oxidation number 0 → +1) and **reduced** to Cl<sup>-</sup> (oxidation number 0 → −1). This is a **disproportionation** reaction.

cards.front_md: Write the ionic equation for the reaction of Cl<sub>2</sub> with cold dilute NaOH and identify which species is oxidised and which is reduced.
cards.back_md:
Cl<sub>2</sub> (aq) + 2OH<sup>-</sup> (aq) → Cl<sup>-</sup> (aq) + ClO<sup>-</sup> (aq) + H<sub>2</sub>O (l)

Cl<sub>2</sub> is **oxidised** to ClO<sup>-</sup> (oxidation number 0 → +1) and **reduced** to Cl<sup>-</sup> (oxidation number 0 → −1). This is a **disproportionation** reaction.

front_blocks.md: When Cl<sub>2</sub> reacts with hot alkali at 70°C, the chlorine is oxidised to chlorate(I) ions (ClO<sup>-</sup>).

back_blocks.md: In hot alkali (70°C), chlorine is oxidised to **chlorate(V) ions** (ClO<sub>3</sub><sup>-</sup>, oxidation number +5), not ClO<sup>-</sup> (+1). Cold alkali produces ClO<sup>-</sup>.

cards.front_md:
**True or False?**

When Cl<sub>2</sub> reacts with hot alkali at 70°C, the chlorine is oxidised to chlorate(I) ions (ClO<sup>-</sup>).
cards.back_md:
**False.**

In hot alkali (70°C), chlorine is oxidised to **chlorate(V) ions** (ClO<sub>3</sub><sup>-</sup>, oxidation number +5), not ClO<sup>-</sup> (+1). Cold alkali produces ClO<sup>-</sup>.

front_blocks.md: Cl<sub>2</sub> reacts with water reversibly: Cl<sub>2</sub> (aq) + H<sub>2</sub>O (l) ⇌ **..........**  (aq) + **..........**  (aq).

back_blocks.md: Cl<sub>2</sub> reacts with water reversibly: Cl<sub>2</sub> (aq) + H<sub>2</sub>O (l) ⇌ **HCl** (aq) + **HClO** (aq).

front_blocks.md: How does chlorine make drinking water safe?

back_blocks.md: Chlorine reacts with water in a disproportionation reaction to form **chloric(I) acid (HClO)**, which **sterilises** water by killing bacteria. HClO can further dissociate to form **ClO**<sup>**-**</sup> (aq), which is also a sterilising agent.

cards.front_md: How does chlorine make drinking water safe?
cards.back_md: Chlorine reacts with water in a disproportionation reaction to form **chloric(I) acid (HClO)**, which **sterilises** water by killing bacteria. HClO can further dissociate to form **ClO**<sup>**-**</sup> (aq), which is also a sterilising agent.

front_blocks.md: In the reaction of Cl<sub>2</sub> with cold NaOH, the oxidation number of Cl in ClO<sup>-</sup> is +1.

back_blocks.md: In ClO<sup>-</sup>, oxygen is −2 and the overall charge is −1, so chlorine must be **+1**. This represents the **oxidation** of Cl<sub>2</sub> (oxidation number 0) in the disproportionation reaction.

cards.back_md:

In ClO<sup>-</sup>, oxygen is −2 and the overall charge is −1, so chlorine must be **+1**. This represents the **oxidation** of Cl<sub>2</sub> (oxidation number 0) in the disproportionation reaction.

front_blocks.md: In the reaction of Cl<sub>2</sub> with hot alkali, chlorine is oxidised to **..........**  (oxidation number +5) and reduced to **..........**  (oxidation number −1).

back_blocks.md: In the reaction of Cl<sub>2</sub> with hot alkali, chlorine is oxidised to **ClO**<sub>**3**</sub><sup>**-**</sup> (oxidation number +5) and reduced to **Cl**<sup>**-**</sup> (oxidation number −1).

front_blocks.md: Write the equation for the further dissociation of HClO in water.

back_blocks.md: Both **HClO** and **ClO**<sup>**-**</sup> act as sterilising agents, making chlorine an effective treatment for drinking water.

cards.front_md: Write the equation for the further dissociation of HClO in water.
cards.back_md:
HClO (aq) → H<sup>+</sup> (aq) + ClO<sup>-</sup> (aq)

Both **HClO** and **ClO**<sup>**-**</sup> act as sterilising agents, making chlorine an effective treatment for drinking water.

front_blocks.md: Write the ionic equation for the reaction of Cl<sub>2</sub> with hot NaOH (70°C).

back_blocks.md: This is a **disproportionation** reaction in which Cl<sub>2</sub> is both **oxidised** (to ClO<sub>3</sub><sup>-</sup>, +5) and **reduced** (to Cl<sup>-</sup>, −1).

cards.front_md: Write the ionic equation for the reaction of Cl<sub>2</sub> with hot NaOH (70°C).
cards.back_md:
3Cl<sub>2</sub> (aq) + 6OH<sup>-</sup> (aq) → 5Cl<sup>-</sup> (aq) + ClO<sub>3</sub><sup>-</sup> (aq) + 3H<sub>2</sub>O (l)

This is a **disproportionation** reaction in which Cl<sub>2</sub> is both **oxidised** (to ClO<sub>3</sub><sup>-</sup>, +5) and **reduced** (to Cl<sup>-</sup>, −1).
